content_notice: DRAFT OPTION CONTENT. Effort ranges are planning placeholders, not measured University figures. Every range carries the assumption it rests on and the evidence that would validate or replace it.

options.capability_gained: A shared written boundary the team can cite: what these tools are used for here, what they are not used for, and where to check when a request sits on the line.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes one drafting pass by a team lead plus one review round with the team, on a team that already has a place to publish internal guidance. Excludes any institution-wide policy negotiation.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: Time recorded against the two most recent comparable internal guidance pages this unit produced, and confirmation that an internal publishing location already exists.

options.observable_indicator: A dated guidance page exists and at least one ticket or thread cites it when resolving a borderline request.

options.capability_gained: A named, non-personal destination for questions about assisted workflows, so the support path does not depend on one individual being reachable.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes an existing queue or channel can be reused and only needs a routing rule and an announcement; assumes no new tooling is procured.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: Confirmation from the service-desk owner that an existing queue can take this traffic, plus the recorded effort of the last routing-rule change.

options.observable_indicator: Questions arrive at the named destination rather than as direct messages, and the destination has a recorded owner that is a role, not a person.

options.capability_gained: A register where a working approach is written down with the task it applies to, so it is reusable by someone who was not in the conversation.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes the register is a page in an existing wiki or documentation system and that seeding it uses approaches the team already has in informal circulation.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: A count of approaches currently circulating informally (from the team's own channel history) and the documentation system's existing page-creation process.

options.observable_indicator: Entries exist, each names the task it applies to, and at least one entry was added by someone other than its originator.

options.capability_gained: A written evaluation note for any new approach trialled, recording the task, the check applied, the result, and the keep-or-drop decision.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes a one-page format agreed once and then reused; excludes the effort of running any particular trial, which belongs to that trial.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: The team's existing change-note or decision-record format, if any, and the recorded effort of adopting the last such format.

options.observable_indicator: At least one completed evaluation note exists naming the task, the check applied, and the decision taken.

options.capability_gained: Hands-on practice on two of the team's own recurring tasks, with the resulting procedures updated to describe the assisted step.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes a team in the range of five to ten contributors, two tasks in scope, preparation by one person and attendance by the rest; assumes no external trainer is engaged.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: The real contributor count for the team, the recorded duration of its last hands-on session of any kind, and whether an external trainer is required by local practice.

options.observable_indicator: A training record names the two tasks practised, and both task procedures have been updated to describe the assisted step.

options.capability_gained: Two recurring workflows mapped end to end, with the points where assistance is permitted and the points where it is excluded both marked in the procedure.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes the two workflows already have some written procedure to amend rather than being mapped from scratch, and that exclusions can be decided inside the team.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: Whether written procedures exist for the two candidate workflows, and whether any exclusion requires sign-off outside the team.

options.observable_indicator: Both procedures show the assisted step and at least one written exclusion with a stated reason.

options.capability_gained: A review cycle over the register so entries carry a last-checked date and stale entries are corrected or retired rather than silently followed.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes a register in the range of twenty to sixty entries and a monthly pass by one reviewer; scales with entry count, not with team size.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: The actual entry count in the register after it has been in use for one quarter, and the time the first review pass takes when measured.

options.observable_indicator: Entries carry a last-checked date, and at least one entry has been corrected or retired as a result of a review.

options.capability_gained: A scheduled evaluation cycle with a known-answer check set, so a change in output quality is detectable rather than inferred from how the output reads.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes ten to twenty check items drawn from work the team has already completed and whose correct answers are already known; excludes building any new tooling.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: Whether completed work with known-correct answers is retrievable for the tasks in scope, and how long assembling the first ten items actually takes.

options.observable_indicator: A check set exists, has been run more than once, and a run has produced a recorded difference that changed a decision.

options.capability_gained: Team-specific guidance covering the data the team actually handles in its own systems, rather than general guidance that leaves the hard cases unresolved.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes coordination with whoever owns the data-handling rules for the systems in question, and one revision round after the first cases surface.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: Identification of the data-handling rule owner for each system in scope, and the turnaround time that owner has needed on comparable requests.

options.observable_indicator: Guidance names the team's own systems and data categories, and a previously unresolved borderline case has been decided by reference to it.

options.capability_gained: An onboarding module covering the assisted steps, so the capability survives staff turnover instead of leaving with the people who built it.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes an existing onboarding process to extend rather than create, and that the procedures updated under OPT-TRN-01 are the source material.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: Whether a documented onboarding process exists for this team, and the recorded effort of the last module added to it.

options.observable_indicator: A person who joined after the module existed completes an assisted task without direct coaching.

options.capability_gained: A written escalation path with a role-level owner, so a question that the first destination cannot answer has a defined next step.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes escalation targets are inside the same organizational unit; a path crossing units would need agreement that is not costed here.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: Where questions that the first destination could not answer actually went over the preceding quarter, taken from the queue record.

options.observable_indicator: The escalation path is written, names roles rather than individuals, and has been used at least once with the outcome recorded.

options.capability_gained: The mapped workflows instrumented so rework is visible, making it possible to see whether an assisted step reduced total effort or moved it downstream.

staff_effort.assumption_basis: Assumes the workflow already passes through a system that can record a rework event; if rework is currently invisible, discovery effort is not included here.
staff_effort.validating_evidence: Whether the systems carrying these workflows already record a reopen, revision, or return-for-correction event, and whether that record is retrievable.

options.observable_indicator: Rework counts for the two workflows are retrievable for a period before and a period after the assisted step was introduced.
